uiLanguage.name: Module language
uiLanguage.hint: Language of First Table on this device. "Like Foundry" follows Foundry's language.

theme.name: Look
theme.hint: Signature shows the card and windows on warm paper. Foundry matches the dark look of Foundry itself.

offer.name: Offer the tour
offer.hint: Who is offered the quick tour without asking. A world that is already in use starts with "Only when I start it for a player".
offer.auto: To new players at their first login
offer.gm: Only when I start it for a player

helpButton.name: Help button
helpButton.hint: Show the small question mark in the controls on the left. It opens the tour, or the player overview for a GM.

tips.name: Fight tips
tips.hint: Show a short tip when the first fight starts and at your first turn. It offers the fight chapter. Tips stop once you know that chapter, and only appear if your GM offers the guide on its own.

offer.title: Hello {name}, new at this table?
offer.text: A quick tour shows you the basics in about three minutes: your sheet, a roll, moving, pinging and the chat. It waits for you at every step, and you can stop whenever you like. More chapters wait behind the question mark in the controls on the left.
offer.invited: Your GM would like to show you around. It takes about three minutes. The tour waits for you at every step, and you can stop whenever you like.
offer.invitedChapter: Your GM would like to show you the chapter "{chapter}". It waits for you at every step, and you can stop whenever you like.

missing.ownToken: None of your tokens is on this scene right now. Skip this step, or wait until your GM puts your token on the map.
missing.otherToken: There is no other token to point at on this scene. Skip this step if you do not want to wait.
missing.canvas: The map is not ready. Skip this step or wait a moment.
missing.combat: No fight is running on this scene. The step waits for the next fight, or skip it.
missing.myCombatant: Your character is not in a fight right now. The step waits for the next fight, or skip it.
missing.myTurn: This step waits for your turn. Skip it if you do not want to wait.
missing.sheetOpen: Open your character sheet first. Show me opens it for you.
missing.rollCard: There is no roll in the chat yet. Roll something first, or skip the step.

menu.title: Guide for new players
menu.experienced: The guide is switched off for you. You can still take any chapter if you like.
menu.intro: Pick a chapter. Each one waits for you at every step, and you can stop and come back any time.

done.title: Those are the basics. Have fun!
done.more: More chapters are waiting. Take the next one now, or come back any time from the question mark in the controls on the left.
done.all: You have been through every chapter. You can play any of them again from the question mark in the controls on the left.

sheet.title: This is your character
sheet.text: Your character sheet holds everything about your hero: abilities, items, spells and notes. You will use it a lot.
sheet.do: Double click your token on the map, or press C, to open your sheet.

roll.title: Roll the dice
roll.text: Almost everything in the game starts with a roll. You roll from your sheet, and the result lands in the chat for everybody at the table.
roll.do: Open your sheet and click something that rolls, for example a skill or an ability. If a small window asks for details, confirm the roll.
roll.doDnd5e: On your sheet click the name of a skill, for example Perception, or an ability like Strength. If a window asks for details, confirm the roll.
roll.doPf2e: On your sheet click the name of a skill or a saving throw. The attack button of a weapon rolls an attack.
roll.doSwade: On your sheet click a skill or an attribute to roll it.
roll.doCrucible: On your sheet click a skill or an action to roll it. The result lands in the chat.
roll.done: Rolled. Everybody can see the result in the chat.

moveKeys.title: Move with the keys
moveKeys.text: Click your token once to select it. Then you can walk it across the map with the keyboard.
moveKeys.do: Press W, A, S and D.
moveKeys.doV13: Press the arrow keys, or W, A, S and D.

moveDrag.title: Move by dragging
moveDrag.text: You can also grab your token and drag it to where you want to go. The ruler shows how far you go.
moveDrag.do: Click your token, hold the button, drag it to another square and let go.

target.title: Pick a target
target.text: Before an attack or a spell you pick your target. A marker shows who you are pointing at.
target.do: Move the mouse over another token and press T, or click it with the target tool in the controls on the left.

ping.title: Ping the map
ping.text: A ping shows everybody what you are talking about. It is the quickest way to say: here, look at this.
ping.do: Press and hold the left mouse button on a spot of the map until a ring appears.

measure.title: Measure a distance
measure.text: How far is it to the door? The ruler tells you.
measure.do: Pick the ruler in the controls on the left, then drag across the map.

chat.title: Say something in the chat
chat.text: The chat on the right is where rolls, messages and the story land. You can write to everybody or to single people.
chat.do: Click the chat box and write a line. To try it quietly, whisper to yourself: type /w, your name and the text.

whisper.title: Whisper to the GM
whisper.text: Whispers are private. Use one to ask your GM something, or to say what your character does in secret.
whisper.do: Type /w gm and your message, for example /w gm Hello!

journal.title: Journals and handouts
journal.text: Maps, notes and handouts your GM shares with you live in the Journal tab of the sidebar. Look there when you want to read something again.
journal.do: Open the Journal tab in the sidebar, the book icon, and open an entry.
journal.done: That is where the story notes live.

sbChat.title: The chat
sbChat.text: Rolls, messages, whispers and the story all land in the chat, each for the people who may see them.
sbChat.do: Click the speech bubble at the top of the sidebar.

sbMode.title: Who sees your roll?
sbMode.text: Next to the chat box you pick who sees your next rolls: everybody, only the GM, only the GM and hidden from you (blind), or only you.
sbMode.textV14: Next to the chat box you pick who sees your next messages and rolls: everybody, only the GM, only the GM and hidden from you (blind), or only you. You can also speak as your character.
sbMode.do: Click one of the small buttons next to the chat box.

sbCombat.title: The combat tab
sbCombat.text: When a fight starts, the combat tracker lists everybody in the order they act. The highlighted name is whose turn it is.
sbCombat.do: Open the Combat tab, the crossed swords.

sbScenes.title: Scenes
sbScenes.text: Scenes are the maps of the game. You see this tab because your GM lets you pick scenes yourself.
sbScenes.do: Open the Scenes tab, the map.

sbPlaceables.title: Placeables
sbPlaceables.text: This tab lists the tokens and other things on the current map that you can see.

sbActors.title: Actors
sbActors.text: Characters and creatures live here. You can open your own character from this list, and others as far as your GM allows.
sbActors.do: Open the Actors tab, the people icon.

sbItems.title: Items
sbItems.text: Items of the game world, like weapons and gear. You see the ones your GM shared. The things your hero carries are on your sheet.
sbItems.do: Open the Items tab, the suitcase.

sbJournal.title: The journal
sbJournal.text: Handouts, maps and notes your GM shares with you. Look here when you want to read something again.
sbJournal.do: Open the Journal tab, the book.

sbTables.title: Roll tables
sbTables.text: Random tables for loot and surprises. The GM usually rolls them, but you may roll the ones shared with you.
sbTables.do: Open the Rollable Tables tab, the list.

sbCards.title: Card stacks
sbCards.text: Stacks of cards, like decks and hands, if your game uses them. It is fine when this tab is empty.

sbMacros.title: Macros
sbMacros.text: Macros are saved little actions that run with one click, like a favorite roll. You can drag them from here to the bar at the bottom.

sbPlaylists.title: Playlists
sbPlaylists.text: Music and sounds of the game. You usually cannot start them, but you decide how loud they are for you.
sbPlaylists.do: Open the Playlists tab, the music note.

sbVolume.title: Your own volume
sbVolume.text: The sliders at the top of the Playlists tab set the volume of music, ambient sounds and interface sounds. They change only your own screen.
sbVolume.do: Move one of the volume sliders.

sbCompendium.title: Compendiums
sbCompendium.text: Compendiums are the libraries of the game: rules, creatures, spells. You see the ones your GM opened for players.
sbCompendium.do: Open the Compendium Packs tab, the atlas.

sbSettings.title: Settings
sbSettings.text: The gears tab holds your personal settings and a few helpful windows, and it is where you leave the game.
sbSettings.do: Open the Settings tab, the gears.

sbConfigure.title: Game settings
sbConfigure.text: Volumes, the look of the interface, the language and many details. These settings are yours alone and change nothing for the others.
sbConfigure.do: In the Settings tab click the button for the game settings, look around and close the window again.

sbControls.title: The key overview
sbControls.text: Every key of the game is listed here, grouped by topic. You can change them, and it is where you find a key you forgot.
sbControls.do: In the Settings tab click the button for the controls and look through the list.

scTokens.title: Token controls
scTokens.text: The bar on the left holds the tools for the map. The button with the person is for tokens: select, target and measure.
scTokens.do: Click the person at the top of the bar on the left.

scSelect.title: The select tool
scSelect.text: This tool selects and moves tokens: click one to select it, drag it to move it. You will use it most.
scSelect.do: Click the select tool, the first tool of the token controls.

scTarget.title: The target tool
scTarget.text: With this tool a click on a token picks it as your target, just like pressing T.
scTarget.do: Click the target tool, the second tool of the token controls.

scRuler.title: The ruler
scRuler.text: Drag across the map with the ruler and the distance appears on the map.
scRuler.do: Click the ruler, the third tool of the token controls.

scShapes.title: Measure shapes
scShapes.text: Circles, cones, rectangles and lines show an area, for example the reach of a spell. Everybody sees what you place.
scShapes.do: Click the button for shapes, below the person button.

scNotes.title: Map notes
scNotes.text: Notes are pins on the map that lead to a journal entry. The bookmark button opens their tools, and the pin tool in there shows or hides them.
scNotes.do: Click the notes button, the bookmark.

scHelp.title: The question mark
scHelp.text: The question mark at the end of the token controls opens this guide. Come back to it whenever you want to play a chapter again.

shOpen.title: Open your sheet
shOpen.text: Your character sheet is your home base. It has tabs, and we look at the important ones now.
shOpen.do: Double click your token on the map, or press C.

shTabs.title: The tabs of the sheet
shTabs.text: The sheet is split into tabs, one for each topic. The one that is open now shows the main facts of your hero.
shTabs.do: Click another tab of your sheet.

shAbilities.title: Abilities and saves
shAbilities.text: Strength, Dexterity and the others are your six abilities. Click the name of one to roll a check or a saving throw.
shAbilities.do: Click the name of an ability on your sheet and confirm the roll.

shSkills.title: Skills
shSkills.text: Skills are what your hero is good at, like Perception or Stealth. A mark shows the skills your hero is trained in.
shSkills.do: Click the name of a skill on your sheet and confirm the roll.

shInventory.title: The inventory
shInventory.text: Weapons, armor, tools, coins and everything else your hero carries. Equipped things count toward your values.
shInventory.do: Open the Inventory tab of your sheet.
shInventory.doSwade: Open the Gear tab of your sheet.
shInventory.doCrucible: Open the tab with your equipment.

shSpells.title: Spells and powers
shSpells.text: Spells and magical powers, and how often you can use them. Casting works like rolling: you click, and the result lands in the chat.
shSpells.do: Open the Spells tab of your sheet.
shSpells.doPf2e: Open the Spellcasting tab of your sheet.
shSpells.doSwade: Open the Powers tab of your sheet.
shSpells.doCrucible: Open the tab with your spells or your grimoire.

shFeatures.title: Features and talents
shFeatures.text: Class features, feats, talents and traits live here: everything your hero can do beyond spells and gear.
shFeatures.do: Open the Features tab of your sheet.
shFeatures.doPf2e: Open the Feats tab of your sheet.
shFeatures.doSwade: Open the Edges tab of your sheet.
shFeatures.doCrucible: Open the tab with your talents.

shItem.title: Look at an item
shItem.text: An item's card shows its description and details. This also works for spells and features.
shItem.do: Right click an item on your sheet and choose View or Edit, or mark this as seen.

shRest.title: Resting
shRest.text: Short and long rests give back hit points and used abilities. You rest when the group does, and your GM tells you when.
shRest.do: Click the button for a short rest on your sheet, then cancel the window without resting.

cdRoll.title: Roll by typing
cdRoll.text: You do not need a sheet to roll. Type /r and a dice formula, for example /r 1d20+3, and press Enter.
cdRoll.do: Type /r 1d20 in the chat box and press Enter.

cdInline.title: Dice inside a message
cdInline.text: A roll in double square brackets becomes a little dice link in your message, and anybody can click it.
cdInline.do: Type I try the door [[/r 1d20]] in the chat box and press Enter.

cdOpen.title: Look at the dice
cdOpen.text: Click a roll in the chat to open it up: every die, the formula and the bonuses.
cdOpen.do: Click the total of a roll in the chat.

cdPrivate.title: Private rolls
cdPrivate.text: A private roll is seen only by you and the GM, a self roll only by you. Everybody else sees nothing of it.
cdPrivate.do: Pick a private mode next to the chat box, then type /r 1d20 and press Enter. Switch back to public afterwards.

cdEmote.title: Emotes
cdEmote.text: Type /em and an action to tell what your character does. It shows in the chat as a line about your character.
cdEmote.do: Type /em shrugs in the chat box and press Enter.

fiTracker.title: The combat tracker
fiTracker.text: It lists everybody in the fight in turn order, with the round at the top. Your character is somewhere in that list.

fiInitiative.title: Roll initiative
fiInitiative.text: Before the first turn everybody rolls initiative, which decides the order. You roll yours from your own entry.
fiInitiative.do: Click the die next to your name in the Combat tab. If a window asks for details, confirm the roll.

fiTurn.title: Whose turn is it?
fiTurn.text: The highlighted entry is whose turn it is. Watch the list so you know when you are next.
fiTurn.do: Look for the highlighted entry in the list. Mark this as seen when you have found it.

fiEnd.title: End your turn
fiEnd.text: When you are done, you end your own turn so the next one can go. The button appears only on your turn.
fiEnd.do: Click the End Turn button in the Combat tab.

fiTarget.title: Target before you act
fiTarget.text: Pick your target before an attack or a spell, so the rolls and effects know whom they are for.
fiTarget.do: Move the mouse over an enemy token and press T.

fiHud.title: The token menu
fiHud.text: A right click on your token opens its menu with quick settings: bars, conditions, elevation and more.
fiHud.do: Click your token with the right mouse button.

fiConditions.title: Conditions
fiConditions.text: Conditions like prone or poisoned show as small icons on the token. The status effects button of the token menu lists them, and a click sets or removes one.
fiConditions.do: Open the token menu and click the status effects button, or mark this as seen.

fiElevation.title: Elevation
fiElevation.text: Flying or climbing? The elevation field of the token menu says how high your token is, if your GM lets you change it.
fiElevation.do: Open the token menu and type a number into the elevation field, or mark this as seen.

exHotbar.title: The macro bar
exHotbar.text: The bar at the bottom has slots, and the number keys run them. You fill them with macros, items and favorite rolls.
exHotbar.do: Click the bar at the bottom, or mark this as seen.

exMacro.title: Make a shortcut
exMacro.text: Drag an item or a skill from your sheet onto a slot of the bar. That makes a macro, and from then on one click uses it.
exMacro.do: Open your sheet and drag an item or a skill onto an empty slot of the bar.

exPlayers.title: The players list
exPlayers.text: The list in the corner shows who is at the table right now. Click it to see offline players too, dimmed. Your color is the color of your pings and rulers.
exPlayers.do: Click the list, or mark this as seen.

exPause.title: Pause
exPause.text: When the GM pauses the game, a big banner says so and nobody moves. Take a breath, the game goes on soon.
exPause.do: There is nothing to click. Mark this as seen.

exAlt.title: Show everything
exAlt.text: Hold the Alt key and Foundry highlights everything on the map you can interact with: tokens, doors and notes. Handy when you cannot find something.
exAlt.do: Hold Alt on the map for a moment, then mark this as seen.

exPing.title: Pings and the GM
exPing.text: You know the ping: press and hold on the map and everybody sees a ring. Only the GM can pull everybody's view to a spot, by holding Shift while pinging. So when your picture suddenly jumps, that was the GM.
exPing.do: Nothing to click, just remember it. Mark this as seen.

scKeys.title: Keys for the tools
scKeys.text: Most tools have a key, like T for targets. The key overview lists all of them, and you can change them.
scKeys.do: Open the Settings tab, click the button for the controls and look through the list.

cdWhisper.title: Whisper to someone
cdWhisper.text: Type /w, a name and your message, and only that person reads it. You can whisper to other players too, not only to the GM.
cdWhisper.do: Type /w and a name, for example your own, then a message, and press Enter.

TourMenu.title: Guide for new players
TourMenu.hint: Shows the chapters of the guide: first steps, sidebar, scene controls, character sheet, chat and dice, fights and extras. A GM sees a preview, nothing is saved.

Overview.title: First Table
Overview.menuHint: See how far every player is in every chapter, offer a chapter to a player, mark players as experienced and choose the chapters and steps.
Overview.hint: New players get the first chapter on their own at their first login. Here you see how far everybody is in each chapter and can offer a chapter to a player.

mode.auto: to new players at their first login
mode.gm: only when you start it for a player

Overview.noPlayers: No players yet. Create users and they appear here.
Overview.start: Offer the first chapter to this player
Overview.startAgain: Offer the first chapter to this player again
Overview.reset: Forget the progress of this player
Overview.invited: {name} will be asked to take the tour.
Overview.stepsHint: Untick a chapter to leave it out for everybody. Open a chapter to untick single steps.
Overview.allExperiencedAsk: Everybody who has not met the tour yet is marked as experienced and will not be offered the tour. Players who already started keep their progress.
Overview.invitedChapter: {name} will be asked to take the chapter "{chapter}".

SELFTEST.Title: Self test
SELFTEST.Hint: Checks after an update that everything the module relies on is there.
SELFTEST.NewVersions: Foundry is newer than the verified version ({versions}). Run the self test if something looks wrong.
SELFTEST.Chat: Foundry's chat styles are built differently than expected. Typed messages are not recognized.
SELFTEST.Sidebar: Foundry's sidebar or key bindings are built differently than expected.
SELFTEST.User: User data cannot be written, so the progress of the tour would be lost.
SELFTEST.Ping: The pings of the map are built differently than expected. The step Ping the map is not recognized.
SELFTEST.Ruler: Foundry's ruler is built differently than expected. The step Measure a distance is not recognized.
SELFTEST.Canvas: The map cannot give screen positions. The ring around tokens is missing.
SELFTEST.Logic: Recognizing the steps and chapters gives wrong results.
SELFTEST.Ui: The sidebar or the scene controls are built differently than expected. The chapters The sidebar and The scene controls cannot point at them.
SELFTEST.Chat2: The chat controls, the macro bar or the players list are missing. Some steps cannot point at them.

DEBUG.Title: Debug file
DEBUG.Hint: One file about all of Sephral's modules in this world, for bug reports. It contains chat text and whispers.
DEBUG.Saved: Debug file saved: {file}. It contains chat text and whispers, check it before you share it.

combatStart.title: A fight begins
combatStart.text: Want a short guide for fights? It shows how to roll initiative, see whose turn it is and end your own turn.

myTurn.title: It is your turn
myTurn.text: Move, act, and then end your turn in the Combat tab. The fight guide shows you where everything is.
